title: Systemic delivery of reprogramming factors
bottleneck: Reprogramming factors are delivered by AAVs, which show strong liver tropism, risk insertional mutagenesis, and can reactivate unexpectedly. Full-body rejuvenation would require reaching muscle, brain, heart, and immune tissues safely, which no current vector achieves; the brain is additionally shielded by the blood-brain barrier.
why_it_blocks: Even a perfect reprogramming protocol is useless without delivery. The vector problem gates the entire rejuvenation field behind a technology that does not yet exist for systemic, transient, safe factor expression.
current_state: AAV-OSKM works in mice for specific tissues (retina, muscle). Non-viral mRNA and small-molecule reprogramming cocktails are early-stage alternatives aiming to avoid genomic integration. Lipid nanoparticles and engineered mRNA offer transient, non-integrating factor expression, but achieving body-wide delivery at therapeutic doses without liver trapping is unresolved.
